video.description_data: ["Being able to reimagine yourself beyond what other people see is the toughest task of all — but it’s also the most beautiful, says journalist Mariana Atencio. In her TED Talk, she explains that the best way to feel like you belong is to embrace what makes you special — and to stay curious about what makes others special, too. “Let’s celebrate those imperfections,” she says. “We are all quirky, and unique, and that is what makes us wonderfully human.”"]

video.description_data: ["Having your own back is not selfish, says meditation advocate Dan Harris — it makes you better at loving other people. In his TED Talk, he shares how he embarked on a journey of self-discovery and self-care when he realized that his family and friends viewed him as kind of a jerk. After starting practices of loving-kindness meditation and positive self-talk, he started to see a huge improvement in his relationships with everyone — including himself. “As your inner weather gets balmier, because you’ve learned how to high-five your demons, that shows up in your relationships with other people,” he explains. “And because relationships are probably the most important variable when it comes to human flourishing, your inner weather improves even further and up you go.”"]

video.description_data: ["Lawyer Bryan Stevenson has dedicated his life to representing the marginalized and wrongly accused and fighting racial discrimination in the US justice system. As human beings, each person’s survival is tied to everyone else’s, he explains in his TED Talk. And we cannot evolve as a society until we deal with inequality. “Ultimately, you judge the character of a society, not by how they treat their rich and the powerful and the privileged,” Stevenson explains, “but by how they treat the poor, the condemned, the incarcerated.”"]

video.description_data: ["This pill-sized robot has the potential to change how doctors see inside your body. In this TED Talk, physician Vivek Kumbhari and engineer Alex Luebke introduce “Pillbot” — a micro-robot that could provide doctors a more direct visualization of your internal organs and potentially spell the end of invasive procedures like endoscopies. Check out their full TED Talk for the entire on-stage demo — including the part where Kumbhari navigates Pillbot *inside* Luebke’s stomach."]
